text: Add the conditional — the one node type that must not evaluate all its children. Fill in the three blanks.
answer: record If(Expr test, Expr then, Expr otherwise) implements Expr { }|eval(f.test(), env) != 0|eval(f.otherwise(), env)
explanation: Verified: with this in place, `def fact(n) = if n < 2 then 1 else n * fact(n - 1); print fact(10);` prints 3628800. Only one branch is evaluated, and that is what makes recursion possible — if both were, `fact` would call itself at the base case too and never terminate. It is the same reason `&&` short-circuits in Java, and why neither can be an ordinary method in a call-by-value language.
